# 2 Maccabees Chapter 15 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Maccabees 15 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/2MA_015_page_001.jpg

---

**15:1** When Nicanor learned that Judas and his men were in the region of Samaria, he resolved to attack them with complete safety on the day of rest.

**15:2** When the Jews who were compelled to follow him said, "Do not destroy so savagely and barbarously, but give honor to the day that the all-seeing has sanctified and exalted above all other days,"

**15:3** the thrice-accursed wretch asked if there were a sovereign in heaven who had commanded the keeping of the sabbath day.

**15:4** When they declared, "It is the living Lord himself, the sovereign in heaven, who commanded the observance of the seventh day,"

**15:5** he replied, "And I am a sovereign also on earth, and I command you to take up arms and carry out the king's business." Nevertheless he did not accomplish his purpose.

**15:6** So Nicanor in his utter boastfulness and arrogance had determined to erect a public monument of his victory over Judas and his men.

**15:7** But Maccabeus never ceased to trust with full confidence that he would receive help from the Lord.

**15:8** He exhorted his men not to fear the attack of the Gentiles, but to bear in mind the former help they had received from heaven and to hope for the victory and aid that would come to them from the Almighty.

**15:9** Encouraging them from the law and the prophets, and reminding them of the battles they had already won, he made them more zealous.

**15:10** When he had aroused their courage, he issued his orders, pointing out at the same time the treachery of the Gentiles and their violation of oaths.

**15:11** He armed each of them not so much with confidence in shields and spears as with the encouragement of good words; and he made them all glad by relating a dream worthy of belief, a sort of vision, that was as follows.

**15:12** He saw Onias, the former high priest, a noble and good man, modest in bearing, gentle in manner, distinguished in speech, and trained from childhood in all things belonging to excellence, with his hands outstretched praying for the whole body of the Jews.

**15:13** Then in the same manner there appeared a man distinguished by his grey hair and dignity, and of marvelous majesty and authority.

**15:14** And Onias spoke, saying, "This is a man who loves the brethren and prays much for the people and the holy city, Jeremiah the prophet of God."

**15:15** And Jeremiah stretched out his right hand and delivered to Judas a golden sword, and in giving it said,

**15:16** "Take this holy sword, a gift from God, with which you will strike down your adversaries."

**15:17** Encouraged by the words of Judas, which were excellent and able to stir the soul to valor and to make the young men's souls strong, they determined not to delay but to make their attack bravely, and to decide the matter by fighting, because the city and the sanctuary and the holy vessels were in danger.

**15:18** For their concern for wives and children and also for brothers and sisters and relatives lay behind this; their greatest and chief fear was for the consecrated sanctuary.

**15:19** And those who were in the city were not troubled of lesser concern, being anxious about the encounter in the open.

**15:20** And when all were now looking for the coming decision, and the enemy had already come near, and the army had been drawn up in battle order, the wild animals having been stationed at a favorable point and the cavalry posted on the flanks,

**15:21** Maccabeus, observing the hosts before him and the various kinds of arms and the fierceness of the wild beasts, stretched out his hands toward heaven and called upon the Lord who works wonders, knowing that victory is not dependent on weapons but that it is his right to give to whom he decides.

**15:22** He called out and said: "You, O Lord, sent your angel in the time of King Hezekiah of Judea and he killed in the camp of Sennacherib one hundred eighty-five thousand.

**15:23** So now also, O Sovereign of the heavens, send a good angel before us to bring terror and trembling.

**15:24** By the might of your arm may those be struck down who with blasphemy have come against your holy people." And with these words he ended.

**15:25** And Nicanor and his men advanced with trumpets and battle songs.

**15:26** But Judas and his men met the enemy with invocations and prayers.

**15:27** Fighting with their hands and praying to God in their hearts, they laid low no fewer than thirty-five thousand and were greatly gladdened by God's manifestation.

**15:28** When the battle was over and they were returning with joy, they recognized Nicanor lying dead in his armor.

**15:29** Then there was shouting and tumult, and they praised the Sovereign Lord in their ancestral language.

**15:30** And the one who had been in every way the chief defender of his fellow citizens, and had maintained from his youth the love of his compatriots, commanded that Nicanor's head and arm, severed from the shoulder, be brought and put on display at Jerusalem.

**15:31** And when he arrived there and had called his compatriots together and stationed the priests before the altar, he sent for those who were in the citadel,

**15:32** and showed them the head of the vile Nicanor and the arm of that blasphemer, which had been stretched out arrogantly against the holy house of the Almighty.

**15:33** And he cut out the tongue of the impious Nicanor and said that he would feed it to the birds bit by bit, and he hung up the fruit of his folly opposite the sanctuary.

**15:34** And all were looking toward heaven and blessed the glorious Lord, saying, "Blessed is he who has kept his own place undefiled."

**15:35** He hung Nicanor's head from the citadel, a signal and plain proof to all of the help of the Lord.

**15:36** And all decreed by common vote never to let this day pass without celebration, but to observe the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which in Aramaic is called Adar, the day before Mordecai's day.

**15:37** Thus matters went with Nicanor, and from that time the city has been in the possession of the Hebrews. And I myself will end my account here.

**15:38** If it has been well narrated and arranged, that is what I was aiming for. If it is cheap and mediocre, that was all I could do.

**15:39** For just as it is harmful to drink wine alone, or again to drink water alone, while wine mixed with water is pleasant and delightful, so the style of the narrative delights the ears of those who read the composition. And with this let it be finished.
